description: Implement a hierarchical file system with directory creation, sorted directory listings, file appends, and file reads. Example 1: create /a/b, add "hello" to /a/b/file, then read that file and receive "hello". Example 2: add " world" to the same file and read "hello world"; listing /a returns ["b"]. Constraints: paths are absolute, components are nonempty, and file operations target valid paths.
intuition: A trie naturally represents path components and lets files and directories share their common prefixes.

brute_force.approach: Store full path strings and scan them to find each directory's immediate children.
brute_force.time: ls O(n), mkdir O(path length), addContentToFile O(path length + content length), readContentFromFile O(1)

optimal.approach: Store child nodes in a trie; each file node owns its content and each directory node owns named children.
optimal.time: ls O(c log c), mkdir O(path length), addContentToFile O(path length + content length), readContentFromFile O(path length)

edge_cases: Listing a file returns only its basename.
Appending to an existing file preserves its earlier contents.
